tiers.title: Entry: one used RTX 3090

price.what: GPU only, used; add a host PC

source.label: insiderllm, GB10 vs Strix Halo vs used 3090

tiers.why: Still the cheapest bandwidth per dollar you can buy. 24GB caps you at ~32B dense.

tiers.title: Two used 3090s: 48GB

price.what: GPUs only, used; needs a 1200W+ PSU and a board with two x8 slots

source.label: insiderllm, GB10 vs Strix Halo vs used 3090

tiers.why: Doubles capacity, not decode speed. The cheapest way to run 70B entirely on GPU.

tiers.title: 128GB unified, cheapest: Strix Halo
tiers.core: Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128GB LPDDR5X (e.g. Bosgame M5)

source.label: insiderllm, GB10 vs Strix Halo vs used 3090

tiers.why: Huge capacity per dollar, low power. Bandwidth is the ceiling: great for MoE, slow on big dense models.

tiers.title: Fastest single card: RTX 5090
tiers.target: Up to 32B at very high speed, image/video gen

price.what: GPU only, US street price; MSRP was $1,999

tiers.why: Unbeatable speed, but at 2×+ MSRP the value is poor and 32GB does not fit 70B Q4.

tiers.title: Quiet and fast unified: Mac Studio M5 Max

source.label: insiderllm, GB10 vs Strix Halo vs used 3090

tiers.why: Best capacity × bandwidth in one silent box. macOS lets the GPU use ~75% of RAM by default.

tiers.title: CUDA in a box: DGX Spark (GB10)
tiers.target: CUDA dev, fine-tuning, 70B+ at modest speed

price.what: complete machine, after the Oct 2 price change

tiers.why: Buy it for the CUDA stack, not for decode speed: bandwidth is similar to Strix Halo at ~2× the price.
